subject: model
value: One row is one content-duplicate group: the single sha256 content hash shared by two or more cataloged files, together with how many files are in the group and the list of their paths.
justification: DDL in sqlite_master declares sha256 TEXT PRIMARY KEY: one row per content hash, with count and paths_json the group's size and membership. builder_path is null, so intent comes from that DDL plus the identical table in the sibling catalog .local/references/research-pdfs/catalog.sqlite, whose single row is count=2 with paths_json ['.local/tiling/hat-spectre/2024 - Smith - A chiral aperiodic monotile - arXiv.pdf', '... arXiv v2.pdf']. That row settles the meaning: paths_json is a member list, one path per duplicate file - a repeating group belonging in a child relation duplicate_set_member(sha256, path) - and count is its derived cardinality. Scope is current-state: a row asserts which paths hold that content now, so moving or deleting one member rewrites paths_json and count under the same sha256. The table is empty here precisely because no two of the 204 audio resources currently share a hash (resources.sha256 has no duplicate value). Not historical - nothing is appended, and the primary key admits only one row per hash. Not per-build - the sibling row persists alongside a catalog that is maintained, not regenerated. Zero rows leaves no atomicity or MVD subjects open, and the declared key is unambiguous.

subject: heading
justification: The stored value is one literal markdown heading line copied verbatim from the indexed document - line 413 of .local/audio/audio-dsp-reference-matrix.md is exactly '## 27. Rolloff, Flatness, Spread, And Spectral Crest', and 46 of the 48 stored headings still match a line of that file byte for byte. subject: title
justification: title is the single section name: the heading with its '## N. ' prefix stripped, which reproduces the stored title in all 48 rows exactly. subject: model
value: One row is the extracted plain-text body of exactly one cataloged resource.
justification: DDL declares resource_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES resources(id) ON DELETE CASCADE: one extracted body per resource, existence-dependent on it. That declaration is the model - the key is the foreign key, so a row cannot outlive its resource; 183 of 204 resources have one. builder_path is null; intent comes from this DDL and the same-shaped document_text table in the sibling catalog .local/references/research-pdfs/catalog.sqlite. text is not an intended key. It is unique across today's 183 extractions by accident of corpus content: this schema explicitly anticipates byte-identical files at different paths (duplicate_sets, populated with a count=2 group in the sibling catalog), and identical files extract to identical text, which breaks it immediately. Nothing in the DDL forbids two resources sharing a body. Scope current-state: text mirrors what the file at resources.path held at extraction time - resources.text_ok, text_chars and text_path record that one extraction - so re-extracting or replacing the file rewrites text under the same resource_id. Nothing is appended or versioned. No atomicity candidates were raised, and text is one archived document body: long, but a single value.

subject: *all-unruled*
justification: 204 rows over 23 columns produce 231 exact FDs from 50 determinants; 48 are sparsity artifacts of two kinds. Near-keys: filename, title, text_path and text_chars are nearly distinct across the corpus, so each trivially fixes everything downstream, and every title,*, sha256,* or creation_date composite is the same effect from pairing a near-unique column with a coarse one. Near-constant targets: notes, pdfinfo_ok and text_ok take very few values, so arbitrary groupings (year->notes, source_group->notes, source_subgroup,text_ok->pdfinfo_ok) fix them by rarity. license, pdfinfo_error and text_error are outright constant, which is why each owns list is 19 wide, not 22. The 10 unlisted determinants are the longest composites, same character. I looked for a real owner and the instance refutes the obvious one: source_subgroup's only dependent is notes, so source_subgroup->source_group does not hold here. sha256 is not a unary determinant (nullable, its NULL bucket collapses), so no content-identity FD was measured. Only id and path own these attributes, and both are DDL-enforced — guaranteed for every future state rather than holding by rarity.

subject: author,pages,year
justification: Near-unique determinant. author is free-text (174 distinct over 178 non-null); the composite yields 185 groups over 204 rows, 182 of them singletons, so 182 rows are alone and cannot test anything. producer is a PDF-toolchain string owned by the file's bytes, not by an author/page-count/year triple: two papers by the same authors in the same year with the same page count may be typeset by different pdfTeX builds. No builder exists for this catalog (packet builder_path is null; grep across the tree found none; it was written ad hoc, evidenced by producer='Codex local review'), so intent was read from DDL plus row semantics only.

subject: creation_date
justification: Free-text pdfinfo timestamp, e.g. 'Thu Jun 29 08:17:24 2023 PDT', with 181 distinct values over 181 non-null rows: fully unique. 182 groups, 181 singletons; the only co-occurring group is the 23-row NULL block (21 directory rows plus the 2 .md analysis-docs), which agrees on author/pages/pdfinfo_ok because that whole block is NULL/0. The dependency is therefore vacuous, and path (the declared key, 204 distinct) already determines all three attributes. A wall-clock second identifies nothing in the modelled world; two PDFs stamped in the same second are ordinary.

subject: creation_date,notes
justification: Same vacuity as creation_date alone, which is already fully unique (181/181 non-null). notes contributes nothing: it holds 2 values, '' on 202 rows and one fixed sentence on 2. 183 groups, 181 singletons. The targets are also near-constant (text_ok is 1 on 183 rows, 0 on 21). A timestamp string paired with a near-constant annotation column is not an entity; this measures the table's sparsity.

subject: creation_date,resource_type
justification: Contains the fully unique creation_date timestamp (181 distinct / 181 non-null), so the composite splits into 186 groups with 181 singletons and the FD is vacuous. resource_type is a 7-value category and categories identify nothing. producer belongs to the file's bytes; it is already determined by path, the declared key, so this adds no constraint the intended key does not already give.

subject: creation_date,resource_type,topic
justification: The clearest sparsity artifact in the packet: three columns, one of them a fully unique free-text timestamp, producing 189 groups over 204 rows with 184 singletons. It 'determines' sha256, size_bytes, text_chars and text_path only because almost every row is alone in its group. All four targets are per-file facts owned by path/content, not by a (timestamp, category, topic) triple; topic has 6 values and resource_type 7, so neither carries identity.

subject: creation_date,text_ok
justification: creation_date is already fully unique among non-null rows (181/181), so text_ok adds nothing: 183 groups, 181 singletons. Both targets are near-constant, notes being '' on 202 of 204 rows and producer NULL on exactly the 21 directory rows. A composite of a timestamp and a boolean extraction flag is bookkeeping, not an entity that owns anything.

subject: creation_date,year
justification: year is largely redundant with creation_date (both come from the same pdfinfo read) and has only 7 distinct values, so the composite inherits creation_date's uniqueness: 186 groups, 184 singletons over 204 rows. text_ok is near-constant (183/21) and producer is byte-owned and already determined by path. Vacuous.

subject: filename -> author,creation_date,id,notes,pages,path,pdfinfo_ok,producer,resource_type,sha256,size_bytes,source_group,source_subgroup,text_chars,text_ok,text_path,title,topic,year
justification: The most seductive false key in this packet. filename is only a base name, undeclared and unenforced; path is the key precisely because base names can collide across source_group/source_subgroup directories in a scraped PDF corpus. It determines everything solely because no collision has yet occurred in 204 rows.

subject: id -> author,creation_date,filename,notes,pages,path,pdfinfo_ok,producer,resource_type,sha256,size_bytes,source_group,source_subgroup,text_chars,text_ok,text_path,title,topic,year
justification: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY surrogate identifier for the catalogued resource. It names a real entity that owns every listed attribute, and the DDL enforces it, so the claim is guaranteed for every future state rather than resting on the current 204 rows.

subject: notes,pages
justification: A composite of a near-constant annotation column and a count. notes has 2 values (202 empty, 2 carrying one fixed generated sentence) and pages has 8 values plus NULL. The target text_ok is itself near-constant, 1 on 183 rows and 0 on 21. It holds because pages IS NULL isolates the 21 directory rows and the 2 .md rows, and notes then separates those two subsets. Counts and free-text notes do not identify anything; a single unreadable PDF with a recorded page count would break it.

subject: notes,pdfinfo_ok
justification: Only 3 groups over 204 rows, all of them composites of near-constant bookkeeping columns: notes has 2 values (202/2) and pdfinfo_ok 2 (181/23). It holds because pdfinfo_ok=1 forces text_ok=1 on 181 rows, and within the 23 pdfinfo_ok=0 rows the notes text separates the 21 directories (text_ok=0) from the 2 annotated .md analysis-docs (text_ok=1). That is a coincidence of two independently near-constant flags plus a 2-value note; nothing here owns text_ok.

subject: pages
justification: There is a real constraint underneath, but it is not this FD and not entity ownership. Measured exactly: pages IS NULL if and only if pdfinfo_ok=0, 181 rows against 23. The builder records a page count only when pdfinfo succeeded, so the content is a null-conditioned/inclusion constraint, not a functional dependency of an entity on its attributes. pages is a count with 8 distinct values (131 rows share the value 8) and identifies nothing; it cannot own an extraction-outcome flag. The FD adds no information beyond the null correlation, and approving it would key a relation on a page count.

subject: pages,text_ok
justification: Composite of a count and a boolean flag determining a near-constant annotation column: notes is '' on 202 of 204 rows and carries one fixed generated sentence on 2. 10 groups, 3 singletons. It holds only because the 2 notes-bearing rows are the .md analysis-docs, which are the sole rows with pages NULL and text_ok=1. Counts and flags do not identify anything, and notes is a hand-written annotation owned by the catalog entry (path), not by a page count.

subject: pages,year
justification: Two bookkeeping counts (8 and 7 distinct values) determining a near-constant flag: text_ok is 1 on 183 rows and 0 on 21. 22 groups, 9 singletons. The 21 zero rows are all directories, which have pages NULL, so the split is driven entirely by the directory/file NULL block rather than by anything year or pages means. One failed text extraction on any DAFx paper would break it.

subject: path -> author,creation_date,filename,id,notes,pages,pdfinfo_ok,producer,resource_type,sha256,size_bytes,source_group,source_subgroup,text_chars,text_ok,text_path,title,topic,year
justification: Declared NOT NULL UNIQUE. The filesystem path is the natural identity the ingest keys on: one path is one catalogued file, and every column here is a fact about that file (its location-derived grouping, its bytes, its pdfinfo, its extraction result). Enforced, so not holding by rarity.

subject: pdfinfo_ok,text_ok
justification: The purest bookkeeping composite in the packet: two booleans yielding 3 groups over 204 rows, determining notes, which has 2 values (202 empty, 2 identical). It holds because the (0,1) group happens to be exactly the 2 generated .md analysis-docs, which are the only rows with a note. Flags do not identify anything; add one .md with an empty note or one PDF that fails pdfinfo but extracts text and it collapses.

subject: producer
justification: producer is a PDF-toolchain label with 23 distinct values (22 pdfTeX builds plus 'Codex local review'), 56 rows on one value. It appears to determine the three targets only through the directory/file split and one coincidence: producer is NULL on exactly the 21 directory rows (all flags 0, notes ''), the 22 pdfTeX values all sit on pdfinfo_ok=1/text_ok=1/notes='', and 'Codex local review' is used by exactly the 2 .md analysis-docs that are the only notes-bearing rows. A typesetter string cannot own per-file extraction outcomes: one corrupt pdfTeX-1.40.25 PDF among the 56 breaks it immediately.

subject: resource_type
justification: All 7 categories are homogeneous in the current rows, but the mechanism is the directory/file split, not ownership. resource_type separates the 21 directory rows (source-tree, matlab-examples, proceedings-folder, book-companion; size_bytes=0, all metadata NULL, both flags 0) from the file rows, and 'analysis-doc' happens to contain exactly the 2 generated .md files that are the only notes-bearing rows. A 7-value category cannot own per-file extraction outcomes: one unreadable PDF among the 178 'proceedings-paper' rows breaks pdfinfo_ok, and one analysis-doc without a note breaks notes. No builder exists to declare it as an invariant (packet builder_path is null and none was found), so this rests on 204 rows alone.

subject: sha256
justification: An accidental superkey, exactly the failure METHOD.md warns about. sha256 has 183 distinct values over 183 non-null rows: fully unique, 183 of its 184 groups are singletons, and the single co-occurring group is the 21-row NULL block of directory rows. No content has ever repeated: duplicate_sets(sha256 PRIMARY KEY) holds 0 rows. So nothing is tested. Decisively, path (declared UNIQUE, 204 distinct) already determines every one of these 10 attributes, so the hash FD adds no constraint the intended key does not give. Two targets are not byte-owned even in principle: text_path is built from the file's path ('<dir>/extracted-text/<stem>.txt'), so identical bytes at two paths would differ, and notes is a hand-written annotation. The defensible direction is path -> sha256, the file owning its hash, which is not what was offered; the sibling authority penrose-reference-index adjudicated this same question as 'The file hash records scan state. It is not the durable identity.'

subject: size_bytes
justification: Near-unique determinant. size_bytes has exactly one colliding value, 0, shared by the 21 directory rows; the other 183 byte counts are all distinct, giving 184 groups with 183 singletons. It therefore determines author, creation_date and notes by uniqueness alone, and the one non-singleton group agrees only because the directory block is uniformly NULL/''. A byte length does not own an author or a creation timestamp; two distinct papers of identical size are permitted by the world and would break it. All three targets already follow from path, the declared key.

subject: title -> author,notes,pdfinfo_ok,resource_type,source_group,source_subgroup,text_ok,topic,year
justification: pdfinfo Title is free text — frequently absent, boilerplate, or a producer artifact. It is a near-unique column, not an entity that owns author/year/topic, and it anchors a whole family of composite artifacts (title,producer / title,creation_date / title,text_path / size_bytes,title) that are the same near-uniqueness restated.
